fields.title: Collections
fields.description: Sets of documents that share a schema, such as pages, posts and products.

data.source:
A collection is a named set of documents with the same fields. Pages, posts, products and categories are all collections. Mortar ships none: your site declares what it needs.

```ts
import { defineCollection, fields } from '@mortar-kit/core';

export const posts = defineCollection({
  name: 'posts',
  label: 'Posts',
  fields: {
    title: fields.text({ label: 'Title', required: true }),
    date: fields.date({ label: 'Published', required: true }),
    excerpt: fields.textarea({ label: 'Excerpt' }),
  },
  body: true,
  sort: { field: 'date', order: 'desc' },
});
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Stable identifier and storage folder. Lowercase, e.g. `posts` or `case-studies`. |
| `label` | The plural name the admin shows. Defaults to `name`. |
| `fields` | The fields every document has. |
| `body` | Whether documents also have a body of bricks. Default `false`. |
| `title` | The text field shown as a document's title in lists. Defaults to the first text field, then the slug. |
| `sort` | The default list order: a field (or `'slug'`) and `'asc'` or `'desc'`. Defaults to the title. |
| `orderable` | Whether editors put the documents in order by hand. Lists then follow that order. Default `false`. See [Manual order](#manual-order). |
| `reservedSlugs` | Slugs documents may not use, such as your own route segments next to `/:slug`. |

## Documents

A document is a plain object:

```ts
interface Doc {
  id: string;        // stable: references store it, and it never changes
  slug: string;      // the address, unique in the collection, e.g. 'hello-world'
  position?: number; // its place in a manual order (orderable collections only)
  fields: { ... };   // the collection's fields
  entries?: PageEntry[]; // the body, when the collection has one
}
```

Slugs are lowercase letters and digits with single dashes between, up to 100 characters. Renaming a slug keeps the id, so links by reference still work.

Keys of `fields` that the schema doesn't describe are kept, so other code can store its own data alongside. Use `DocOf<typeof posts>` for a typed document.

## Manual order

Some sets are curated rather than sorted: photos, a timeline, project cards. Make the collection `orderable` and editors put its documents in order in the admin, by dragging a row of the document list or with its move up and down buttons.

```ts
export const projects = defineCollection({
  name: 'projects',
  label: 'Projects',
  fields: { title: fields.text({ label: 'Title', required: true }), image: fields.image({ label: 'Image' }) },
  orderable: true,
});
```

- Lists return documents in that order: `content.list(projects)` needs no `sort`. Pass a `sort` to order them another way for one list.
- New documents go to the end.
- The order is kept in each document's `position` (1, 2, 3…), next to its `id`, so it works with every store, the JSON files included, and shows up in git diffs. `createContent` manages it: saves keep the stored position (a stale editor can't undo a move), and `content.move(collection, id, index)` moves a document, rewriting only the documents whose position changes. Nobody types a position.
- Collections without `orderable` work as before, sorted by `sort`.

### Making an existing collection orderable

Nothing to migrate. Documents without a position come after those with one, in the collection's `sort` order, so a collection you make orderable keeps its current order. The first move, or the first save of a new document, gives every document a position in that order (one write per document, once). Files you add by hand without a position join the end the same way.

If your app wraps `Content` for the admin (as the example's server functions do), add `move` to the wrapper: without it the admin shows no reorder controls.

## Many collections, one admin

Pass them all to `<Admin>` in the order its rail should list them, and to `createContent`, which checks that every reference field names a known collection.

```ts
export const collections = [pages, posts, products, categories] as const;
```
